notes: Wigan Council does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: you need a licence if five or more people from two or more households share the property. The fee is £823 for a new application and £531 to renew.
research: Wigan's complete licensing taxonomy contains exactly six categories: Animals, Business and Trading, Entertainment/Alcohol/Late Night Refreshments, Gambling, HMO, and Taxi and Private Hire. There is no housing licensing category other than HMO, and within it the only application route offered is 'Applying for a mandatory HMO Licence'. The HMO page states: 'All properties occupied by five or more individuals from two or more households, sharing amenities, must obtain a mandatory licence, regardless of the number of storeys.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'New application - £823', 'Renewal application - £531', 'Properties with 11 to 20 occupiers will pay an additional fee of £34', 'Properties with 21 and above occupiers will pay an additional fee of £65.' A single occupancy-banded mandatory ladder with no per-dwelling fee and no separate application route. The word 'selective' appears zero times on the fees page. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) THE BEST NEW TRAP IN THE PROJECT. The string 'Selective licensing' DOES appear on the Private Landlords page, but ONLY at byte offset 522 inside a meta keywords tag: 'content="...Landlord duties,Landlord responsibilities,Selective licensing,landlords,Landlords Wigan..."'. It is an SEO keyword in the page head, never in the body, and the page's actual services are Landlord Hub, Landlord duties, Housing Benefit Portal, HMO licence and Ethical Lettings Agency. This would fool any keyword-matching scraper into reporting Wigan as positive. (2) The HMO further-information page contains two 'selective' hits, both inside an external GOV.UK href for the First-tier Tribunal appeal form, 'form-hmo-applications-relating-to-licensing-of-houses-in-multiple-occupation-hmos-and-selective-licensing', the exact GOV.UK-URL trap seen at Stafford. (3) 'Ethical Lettings Agency' is an in-house lettings and landlord incentive service, not Part 3. (4) The £34 and £65 additional fee lines are surcharges on a mandatory licence. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing from Manchester, Salford or Bolton was relied on. LIMITATIONS: Wigan's /sitemap.xml is a 1,104-byte stub listing only 5 URLs, so the sitemap sweep was useless and the taxonomy was crawled directly instead. Wigan's site search is Cludo; the api.cludo.com endpoint returned HTTP 401 to every request including the controls, so no site-search test was run and no evidence is claimed from it. The 'Do I need to apply for a licence' page returns a 500 Internal Server Error. The ward boundary review question is not engaged as there is no designation.

notes: Winchester City Council does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for properties let to five or more people from two or more households. The licence fee is £1,247 and renewal £983 from 1 April 2026.
research: The HMO page states: 'From 1 October 2018, the law (The Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Prescribed Descriptions) (England) Order 2018) requires all multi-occupied dwellings with 5 or more occupants living as more than one household to be licenced.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'HMO Licensing Fee - £1201 (£1247 as of 1st April 2026)', 'Re-Licensing Fee - £947 (£983 as of 1st April 2026)', split into an administration element of £511 (£528) new and £257 (£264) renewal payable on submission, and a management element of £690 (£719). One mandatory fee only, no per-dwelling cost-recovery fee and no second application route, so no self-financing discretionary scheme exists. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned 1,754 URLs; the word 'selective' appears zero times across the whole file. METHOD NOTE WORTH RECORDING: the sitemap uses http:// rather than https:// URLs, which defeated a protocol-anchored grep on the first pass; it was re-run protocol-agnostically before concluding. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Two Article 4 Direction pages covering Stanmore and Winnall, plus news items 'council-to-tighten-controls-on-hmos' (2016) and 'tighter-planning-controls-in-winnall-set-to-control-the-rise-in-houses-of-multiple-occupation' (2018). These are planning controls over C3-to-C4 conversion, not licensing designations, and they name areas and dates which is exactly why they get misread. (2) THE DECISIVE POSITIVE EVIDENCE FOR THE NEGATIVE: the Winchester Shared Housing Accreditation Scheme is explicitly 'voluntary' and is aimed at 'smaller HMOs of between 3 - 4 tenants which fall outside of the mandatory licensing requirement'. That wording is itself proof that no additional licensing scheme exists, because under a s.56 designation those 3-4 tenant HMOs would be licensable rather than merely accreditable. (3) The news item 'hmo-licensing-powers-to-come-into-force-in-october' (2018) is the national mandatory extension, not a local designation.

notes: The Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to five or more people from two or more households. The fee is £920.70 for a first property of up to five bedrooms.
research: RBWM's site is at rbwm.gov.uk. The 'do you need an HMO licence' page states a licence is needed where 'It is occupied by five or more persons who consist of two or more households'. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'First property (with up to 5 bedrooms): £920.70', 'Second and subsequent properties: £847.00', 'Additional fee per extra bedroom (after five bedrooms): £30.80', 'Renewal of licence and second and subsequent properties: £847.00', plus a £50.00 hourly rate for incomplete applications and £11.18 for a duplicate licence. A fee ladder whose base band is 'up to 5 bedrooms' with a per-bedroom surcharge only above five is the textbook mandatory-only signature; there is no per-dwelling flat fee and no separate scheme application route. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is a Drupal simple_sitemap index pointing to three sub-sitemaps; expanded, these gave 5,547 URLs. The word 'selective' appears zero times in the whole set. The only HMO-related pages are the six under the houses-multiple-occupation branch (about, apply, do-you-need, regulations-summary, renew, report) plus an HMO privacy notice; there is no selective or additional licensing page. TRAPS EXCLUDED: 'Additional fee per extra bedroom' is a surcharge on a mandatory licence, not s.56. The 'about houses in multiple occupation' page contains zero 'selective' hits. No Article 4 or accreditation material was mistaken for licensing.

notes: Wokingham Borough Council does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, which since 1 October 2018 covers any property let to five or more people from two or more households sharing facilities.
research: The HMO page states: 'On 1 October 2018 the mandatory licensing scheme was extended to HMOs that are: ... Occupied by five or more occupants'. The word 'selective' appears zero times on that page. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned 2,517 URLs with zero occurrences of 'selective' anywhere in the file. The complete private housing subtree is only eight pages (private-housing, houses-multiple-occupation-hmo, private-housing-explained, private-housing-policy, private-rented-scheme, register-hmo-licences, reporting-housing-issues and smoke-alarm-and-carbon-monoxide-regulations) with no selective or additional licensing page and no second licence application route. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) The 'private rented scheme' page sounds like a licensing scheme but is a landlord incentive and Local Housing Allowance rate page; its content is a rent table reading 'Room in any shared accommodation: £390.43 pcm', '1 bedroom: £847.69 pcm', '2 bedrooms: £1092.00 pcm', '3 bedrooms: £1296.45 pcm', '4 bedrooms: £1649.48 pcm'. This is the 'selective lettings / landlord incentive scheme' trap and is not Part 3. (2) The 'private housing policy' page is a home improvement loans policy for owner-occupiers over 60 (loans up to £20,000), not a licensing policy. LIMITATION: no separate published HMO fee table was located on the Wokingham site, so the fee-schedule test here rests on the absence of any second application route rather than on a quoted mandatory fee line; the sitemap and page-body evidence for the negative is nonetheless direct and complete.

notes: City of Wolverhampton Council does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to five or more people from two or more households. The application fee starts at £977 for an HMO of up to six bedrooms.
research: FLAGGED AS THE MOST LIKELY POSITIVE IN THIS BATCH AND IT IS A NEGATIVE, established from Wolverhampton's own domain by three independent methods and then INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED BY THE COORDINATOR via direct fetch with a browser user-agent (raw-HTML 'selective' count on the HMO page: zero). (1) SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is an index of two sub-sitemaps, both carrying lastmod 2026-08-05T10:43Z, i.e. regenerated the same day it was checked, so it is not stale. Expanded, it contains 10,321 URLs. The word 'selective' appears ZERO times anywhere in the file. Every 'additional' hit is unrelated (COVID Additional Relief Fund, second homes premiums, library consultation, adult learners with additional needs, savings proposals). The only housing licensing page in the entire estate is the HMO licence page with five children (change of circumstances, variation, change of address, surrender or close a MANDATORY licence, temporary exemption). (2) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the definition given is 'A HMO requires a mandatory property licence when all the below apply: it is occupied by 5 or more persons regardless of age from 2 or more households'. The fee structure is 'costs relating to the processing of an application for an HMO up to 6 bedrooms, up to and including the decision to grant or decline. £977' with add-on bands for 7 to 10, 11 to 20, 21 to 30 (£158), 31 to 40 (£220), 41 to 50 (£281) and 'For each incremental 10 bedrooms', split into 'Fee 1 Application processing and determination fee' and 'Fee 2 - Licence scheme operation and enforcement fee', plus £7 per non-HMO part of the building, £28 for commercial areas and £82 for a copy of the public register. A ladder whose base band is 'up to 6 bedrooms' against a five-occupant threshold, with no per-dwelling flat fee, is decisive evidence of mandatory-only. (3) SITE SEARCH WITH CONTROLS, which PASSED: 'selective licensing' returned 'Results 0 - 0 of 0'; the positive control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 'Results 1 - 2 of 2'; the nonsense negative control returned 'Results 0 - 0 of 0'. All three responses had different byte lengths and different md5 hashes, proving the engine discriminates and can genuinely return zero. TRAPS EXCLUDED: Wolverhampton runs a voluntary 'Rent with Confidence' private landlord star-rating scheme; this is accreditation, not licensing. Its many rogue-landlord prosecution news items concern mandatory HMO offences. No Birmingham, Sandwell or Walsall material was relied on. LIMITATION: the ModernGov committee search is unusable without ASP.NET viewstate; both GET and POST attempts returned byte-identical responses for 'selective licensing', 'housing' and a nonsense term, so it FAILED the control test and no inference is drawn from it either way. An unpublicised committee proposal therefore cannot be fully excluded, but there is no live or lapsed scheme on the public site.

notes: Worthing Borough Council does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to five or more people forming more than one household. The fee is £810 on application plus £55 for each unit above five.
research: Worthing shares a website and services with Adur District Council at adur-worthing.gov.uk, so the first question was whether the licensing position is stated jointly. It is: the single HMO page is headed 'Houses in Multiple Occupation - Adur and Worthing Councils' and describes one mandatory regime covering 'the Adur and Worthing area', with a licence required where 'five or more persons are living there as more than one household'. No separate Worthing-only scheme or fee exists. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, quoted from that page: 'Standard HMO Licence Fee and Re-Licence Fee', 'Fee on application: £810', 'Fee on grant of licence: £485', 'An additional Fee on application of £55 is payable for each unit of accommodation over five', worked through as '7 bed shared house: £810 + (2 x £55) = £920', '8 bedsit property with shared bathrooms: £810 + (3 x £55) = £975', '5 bedsits with shared shower rooms and 6 self-contained flats: £810 + (6 x £55) = £1,140', with the grant element 'fixed at £470 per licensed property'. A surcharge that begins only above five units is the mandatory-only signature; there is no per-dwelling fee and no second application route. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is 404, but the HTML sitemap at /site-map/ returns 114,549 bytes and lists the full estate. The word 'selective' appears ZERO times in it. The housing subtree contains exactly one HMO page and no selective or additional licensing page. The landlords section contains only account sign-up, advice, NRLA, receiving benefits payments, the Renters' Rights Act 2025 and view account. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Shared-service bleed with Adur: the joint page was confirmed to be mandatory-only for BOTH authorities rather than assuming Worthing follows Adur. (2) Neighbour bleed from Brighton and Hove, which does run schemes, was not relied on at any point. (3) The 'additional Fee on application' line is a surcharge, not s.56. (4) Both Private Sector Housing Assistance Policy PDFs were downloaded and contain zero 'selective' strings, though note that PDF text-stream compression makes a string scan of a PDF weaker evidence than the HTML findings, which are the basis for this record. Worthing's substantial bedsit stock made this a plausible positive, but there is no designation, current or lapsed, published anywhere on the council's own domain.

notes: Wychavon District Council states that it operates mandatory HMO licensing only, with no selective or additional scheme. You need a licence if you let to five or more people who are not one household and who share facilities. Fees start at £820.
research: Wychavon gives an explicit, unambiguous statement of its position, the strongest form of evidence for a negative. The HMO page reads verbatim: 'Wychavon District Council operates mandatory HMO licensing. If you rent a property to five or more people, not from the same household and they share facilities you must have a HMO licence. This is regulated under the Housing Act 2004 and has been in force since 2006.' The word 'selective' appears zero times on the page. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the page carries an occupancy-banded ladder of £820 / £750, £1,225 / £1,159, £1,427 / £1,361, £1,630 / £1,567, and a second set at £642 / £576, £1,050 / £984, £1,251 / £1,190, £1,457 / £1,392 (new and renewal pairs), with the accompanying standards text 'The minimum room sizes for HMO properties with 5 or more sharing are'. A ladder keyed to five-or-more occupancy with no per-dwelling flat fee is mandatory-only. The single application route is the council's own self-service portal; there is no second route that a discretionary scheme would require. The housing section contains only disabled facilities grants, empty homes, the empty homes hub, energy efficiency, homelessness, HMOs, housing advice, housing for you, the housing needs study and a severe weather protocol. TRAPS EXCLUDED: shared-service bleed. Wychavon sits in South Worcestershire shared arrangements alongside Malvern Hills and Worcester, and Wyre Forest is also in this batch, so Wychavon's position was established solely from its own domain, its own wording and its own fee table rather than reading across from any partner authority. LIMITATION WORTH RECORDING AS A METHOD NOTE: wychavon.gov.uk sits behind a Sucuri WAF that returns an HTTP 307 to a self-referencing JavaScript challenge for every request, so every URL superficially looks like a redirect loop and a naive check would report the whole council unreachable. The base64 challenge payload was decoded, the sucuri_cloudproxy cookie computed and replayed to reach the real pages. This is a bot block, not evidence of anything about licensing.

notes: Wyre Council does not run selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for properties occupied by five or more people. Wyre does have an Article 4 direction for HMOs, but that is a planning control and not a licensing scheme.
research: Wyre covers Fleetwood and neighbours Blackpool, which definitely does run schemes, so this needed care. It is a negative. The HMO page states: 'All properties that are occupied by five or more people require a mandatory House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) licence.' The housing enforcement page states: 'Investigation may also be undertaken to identify those houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) that are required to be licensed under Part II Housing Act 2004. Landlords of those HMOs that come within the scope of the licensing requirements but have failed to seek a licence will be advised accordingly.' The council describes its licensing duty exclusively by reference to Part 2 mandatory licensing; there is no reference anywhere to Part 3 or to s.56. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned 5,089 URLs (the bare /sitemap also resolves). The word 'selective' appears ZERO times across the whole file. The only HMO pages are the main HMO page and its two pagination children, a change form, and an HMO standards download. TRAPS EXCLUDED, and this is the important one: Wyre has an 'Article 4 Direction for HMOs' published in two places, with an Evidence Document, a Map, a Direction Notice and a Notice of Confirmation. It was fetched and confirmed to be filed under 'Planning and building control'. It is a removal of permitted development rights for C3-to-C4 conversion, not a licensing designation. Because it names an area, has a commencement date and comes with a map and confirmation notice, it is precisely the artefact most often misreported as a selective licensing scheme, and Wyre's terraced Fleetwood stock makes that misreading especially tempting. Also excluded: the various landlord portal URLs are Housing Benefit direct-payment portals, not licensing. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing from Blackpool was relied on. LIMITATION: one HMO sub-page returned only site navigation when fetched, so the finding rests on the main HMO page and the enforcement page instead; no published HMO fee figure was located for Wyre, so the fee-schedule test here rests on the absence of any second application route rather than a quoted fee line.

notes: Wyre Forest District Council does not run selective or additional licensing. Its HMO policy states that conditions in the district do not warrant a scheme, and that it keeps this under review. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, with a fee of £880.
research: METHOD NOTE FIRST: Wyre Forest District Council's website is at wyreforestdc.gov.uk; the obvious guess wyreforest.gov.uk does not resolve at all, which would strand a checker that assumed it. The published HMO Policy gives an explicit determination against designation, the strongest possible evidence for a negative. Section 7, headed 'Selective/Additional Licensing', reads: '7.1 The Housing Act 2004 and regulations made there under make provision for additional or selective licensing. This means that other HMOs and rented accommodation can be brought into a licensing scheme. However this can only be done in certain very limited circumstances...' and concludes 'The current circumstances in the District do not warrant and would not therefore be successful in an application for selective/additional licensing. This situation will be kept under review.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the HMO page gives a licence required 'if the property is inhabited by five or more people' and 'The licence fee is currently set at £880.00', rising to £1,160.00 where an incomplete application must be resubmitted. A single mandatory fee, no per-dwelling cost-recovery fee, no second route. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is 404 and /robots.txt is absent, but the bare /sitemap resolves and returned 389,419 bytes covering the whole estate, with ZERO occurrences of 'selective'. TRAPS EXCLUDED, three of them: (1) The policy's section 7 is a STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL that describes the discretionary power and then expressly declines to exercise it. Read by title or by keyword hit alone, a page containing the heading 'Selective/Additional Licensing' five times looks like a positive; read in the body it is the opposite. It also cites 'The Selective Licensing of Houses (Specified Exemptions) (England) Order 2006', a statutory reference, not a designation. (2) A 'Non-Immediate Article 4 Direction in Kidderminster', fetched and confirmed: 'On Friday 20 February 2026 Wyre Forest District Council introduced a Non-immediate Article 4 Direction within the Town of Kidderminster, removing the permitted development right to convert a dwellinghouse (Class C3) into an House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) (Class C4)... Conversions of dwellings to HMOs for seven or more residents continue to require planning permission.' Planning control, very recent, names a town and a commencement date, and is the single most likely thing in this council to be misreported as a licensing designation. (3) Fourteen 'local lettings plans' (Berrington Court, Carpets of Worth, Catchems End Bewdley, Emery Court, Habberley Park, Husum Way, Mortimer Manor, Parsons Chain, Pearl Lane, Sandbourne Gardens, Station Drive Blakedown, Stourport High School, The 1902 Building) are social housing allocation instruments, not Part 3. Also excluded: standard civil-penalty boilerplate on the HMO page referring to prosecution with an unlimited fine, penalties up to £30,000 and Rent Repayment Orders, which exist regardless of whether any discretionary scheme is designated. Shared-service bleed with Wychavon and the wider Worcestershire arrangements was avoided by sourcing everything from Wyre Forest's own domain and own policy.
